references.text: The direct Old Testament background for Jesus' words. Moses made a bronze snake and set it on a pole, and all who looked at it after being bitten by snakes were healed. Jesus compares his own exaltation (crucifixion) to this event ([ref:Num 21:8-9|Numbers 21:8-9]).

Jesus says: "When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will understand that I AM." Here the same Greek word ὑψόω (to lift up/exalt) is used, pointing to the crucifixion as an exaltation ([ref:John 8:28|John 8:28]).

Jesus says: "When I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to myself." Again ὑψόω is used, and John explains explicitly that Jesus said this to show what kind of death he would die ([ref:John 12:32-34|John 12:32-34]).

Paul describes how Christ, after his humiliation and obedience unto death on the cross, was exalted by God and given the name above every name. The exaltation on the cross leads to exaltation in glory ([ref:Phil 2:8-9|Philippians 2:8-9]).

The immediate purpose of the Son of Man's exaltation is explained: "so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life." Just as the bronze snake brought physical healing to those who looked at it, the exalted Christ brings eternal life to those who believe ([ref:John 3:15-16|John 3:15-16]).

Isaiah's prophecy about the Lord's suffering servant who shall be "exalted and lifted up and be very high" – a prophecy pointing toward Christ's exaltation through suffering ([ref:Isa 52:13|Isaiah 52:13]).

Jesus refers to himself as "the Son of Man" (τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου), a title he consistently uses in the Gospel of John, drawn from [ref:Dan 7:13|Daniel 7:13]. Here he reveals his heavenly identity ([ref:John 1:51|John 1:51]).

Jesus asks: "What then if you see the Son of Man ascend to where he was before?" This links the exaltation of the Son of Man to his ascension and his origin with the Father ([ref:John 6:62|John 6:62]).

"He who knew no sin, God made to be sin for us." Just as the bronze snake bore the image of sin (the form of a serpent) without itself being poisonous, Christ bore the judgment of sin without himself having sinned ([ref:2 Cor 5:21|2 Corinthians 5:21]).

"Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree." The exaltation on the cross was a curse that brought salvation ([ref:Gal 3:13|Galatians 3:13]).
